notes: CLI route (post-build): Next.js 16 builds with Turbopack by default (webpack with next build --webpack), and there is no Bugsee Next.js config wrapper yet, so the wizard adds a post-build step that works for either bundler: scripts/bugsee-sourcemaps.mjs runs bugsee-cli on the .next output after the build to inject debug ids and upload the source maps (the 'bugsee:sourcemaps' script is chained into "build"). The step needs source maps to exist: set productionBrowserSourceMaps: true in next.config (the wizard does not edit it); without it the browser bundles have no maps and only the server output is uploaded. The output directory is .next; if next.config sets distDir (or output: 'export', which writes out/), change the directory in the 'bugsee:sourcemaps' script. The app token comes from BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN or .env.bugsee-build-plugin; with no token it skips with a warning. Next serves .next/static as built, so the browser .map files stay public unless you delete them after the upload (for example find .next/static -name '*.map' -delete). Initialising the SDK for Next.js is not automated by the wizard yet: follow the @bugsee/nextjs setup (instrumentation.ts and instrumentation-client.ts).
verify: Verify symbolication in a production build: serve or deploy it (not the dev server), trigger a test error from it (for example a button that throws new Error('Bugsee test error')), then open the report in the Bugsee dashboard. The stack should show your original files, functions and lines; minified positions such as a.js:1:48210 mean the source maps were not uploaded for this build or do not match it.

For Next.js, run your package build script (for example npm run build: it chains the source map upload, which running Next's own build command directly skips) then next start, and trigger a test error both from a client component and from a server route or server component.
